result.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
result.summary: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene content from clips with low initial anomaly scores and uses this estimate to partially correct the textual reference. It then rescales category responses, penalizes clips with strong responses across categories, and refines the anomaly directions using high-scoring clips. VIDE averages scores across prompt views to reduce sensitivity to prompt selection and fuses scores from two frozen encoders. With both encoders, VIDE improves AUC over the best PRISM result by $1.5$, $1.9$, and $3.5$ points on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD, respectively, and AP by $6.5$ points on XD-Violence and $9.3$ points on MSAD. VIDE yields the highest AUC among the compared training-free methods on all three benchmarks and the highest reported AUC among all compared methods on XD-Violence and MSAD. Our code is included in the supplementary material and will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练视频异常检测框架 VIDE：基于冻结 CLIP 嵌入，用初始低异常分片段估计各测试视频的正常场景内容，据此局部修正文本导出的正常性参考、重标定类别响应并精化异常方向，再对多个提示视角与两个编码器的分数进行融合。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「困难/高相似片段带来的异常偏置」、提示选择敏感性及按视频用视觉证据校正文本参考的做法，可能与 LVR 中 latent 相似度评分受内容与文本偏置影响、视觉证据筛选与打分校准的问题相通，可供核查；但论文本身不涉及推理状态生成或动态计算，迁移性待验证。
